o1.biggest_strength: Every script earns its angle from my data (blind taste and swap lead, label only after the taste), and the $3 pushback is answered inside Script 2 with a real reason instead of a discount.
o1.biggest_mistake: It never tells me which script to shoot first and leaves out production specs (deliverables, rights, caption burn-in, safe framing), so I still have homework before I can hand it to a creator.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add a shoot order and a one-page production spec pack to the creator briefs, and test the price objection as one of the alternate hooks.

o2.biggest_strength: It reads like a producer's packet: an explicit shoot-first call, price doubt and habit tested as named hook types drawn from real comments, disclosure baked into every script plus a shared brief with deliverables, rights and framing.
o2.biggest_mistake: Script 3 shortens the approved claim to "real fruit juice" and drops "and botanical flavours," and calls TikTok's tool a "paid partnership label" when it is the branded content toggle.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Quote every approved claim in full and add the same nine-way, same-budget hook test plan its competitor has, so I know exactly how to pick a winner.

reason: Both pick the right three angles and get $35.99, $3 a can and the cost-per-purchase ranking right, but #2 is the one I can forward to creators today: it names the first script to shoot and carries disclosure, deliverables, rights and safe framing, where #1 leaves me to build the production side myself.
